KIDS HOOKED ON CODEINE

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Kids are hooked on a codeine cooldrink cocktail – available over the counter for less than 50 bucks. We investigate the cracks in the system and expose some of the dodgy suppliers.

Unique Selling Point:
* RELEVANT TO VIEWERS
* UNDERCOVER INVESTIGATION
* LEKKER BUSTS
* CONFRONTS WITH AUTHORITIES

Summary:
Codeine based cough mixtures are the latest source of high for South African youth. It’s been popularised by international hiphop culture and even amongst local musicians.

It’s easy to get. It’s easy to hide. It’s easy to get hooked.

We investigate this dangerous trend and go undercover the expose the culprits selling unregulated quantities of cough mixture.


Further information:
There are a range of street names for this concoction - Lean, Dirty Sprite, Sizzurp, Purple Drank… call it what you want, but it all comes down the same dangerous mixture gripping South African youth.

WHAT IS IT?
Usually 1/2 bottle of cough syrup per 2 litre of flavoured cool drink.

Different kinds of cough mixtures are used because they have different amounts of codeine – for example - Benylin has the highest percentage of Codeine in it, while Stilpane contains both Codeine and Promethazine. Promethazine is an antihistamine that causes sedative effects and can impair motor functioning 2.

WORD FROM USERS
- “When I don’t drink it, I don’t feel good about myself, everything feels tense and uneasy but the moment I sip some, my whole body just calms down” – Marketing student
- “It makes me relax, when I’m on lean, I feel calm and lazy. I don’t want to do anything but chill, ’’ – 20yr old student
- “Yes, I’m aware of the dangers but it’s hard to stop drinking lean,”

STATS ON CODEINE ADDICTION
2.1% of people admitted to drug treatment centres in SA reported the non-medical use of codeine in 2017, this is according to a South African Medical Research Council (SAMRC) study published in the South African Medical Journal.

WHAT’s BEING DONE TO GET A GRIP ON CODEINE ADDICTION
Codeine control
A national SAMRC survey conducted in 2014 reported that less than half (42%) of pharmacists believed the level of control of codeine in the pharmacies they worked in was high enough.

The Codeine Care Initiative – BIG TALK – NO ACTION
The project was implemented by the Community Pharmacy Sector and the Pharmaceutical Society of South Africa in 2013, showed enormous promise.

It put a system in place which necessitates the name of the person buying codeine to be registered by a pharmacist in an attempt to help regulate the sale and distribution of medicines that contain this drug.

But it appears not to have had the level of support from the retail pharmacy sector it needs to be effective.

CAN’T WITHDRAW FROM MARKET
Codeine-containing medicine has a very important place in the treatment of day to day ailments and making this inaccessible would just put additional burden on our health system. The abuse of codeine by a relatively small percentage of people could lead to other effective medicine not being available to the rest of the population who uses it responsibly if it were to be withdrawn.
International regulation of codeine
Australia is not unique in its requirements to have a prescription for codeine containing products. Countries in Europe including Austria, Belgium, France, Germany and Italy, well as the United States, Japan, Russia, and the United Arab Emirates all require prescriptions for medicines containing codeine. In some other countries including Hong Kong, Hungary and the Netherlands, OTC sale of cough linctus (containing codeine) is allowed, with all other medicines containing codeine requiring a prescription. Most recently the new French Government announced in July 2017 that all medicines containing codeine would only be available via prescription.

Most recently, in January 2018, the Nigeria and Kenya announced that all medicines containing codeine have been rescheduled to Prescription Only Medicines. Canada and New Zealand are also currently considering whether to make codeine medicines Prescription Only.
LEGALLY
In South Africa, pharmacies are legally required to keep records of dispensed scheduled 2 medication – but this doesn’t happen – and is not enforced.

DURBAN YOUTH HOOKED HARD
The Coloured community of Wentworth is fighting a war against codeine addiction. You’ll find piles of bottles in the streets. Kids zonked on the concoction every day – it’s easy to take because it looks like cooldrink.

Sister Rennette works at hospital during the day and at a rehab centre attached to the church in the evening – she has seen the impacts first hand and will show us around the neighbour sharing stories of the devastating affects.

Terence Flynn is a recovered addict and dealer – he will help up us exposed a supplier that sells large quantities of cough mixtures for illegal distribution by drug dealers.

CASE STUDY 1
Sunny is a 20 year guy – starting a career on local community TV in the music industry – he takes it regularly and will explain how common it is in the music industry and amongst his friends – they don’t think it’s a problem because it’s not illegal drugs nor is it booze.

CASE STUDY 2
Sister Rennette will arrange for us to speak to a 16 year old boy that has just started coming to rehab – he is not clean yet. Don’t know too much about his story yet.

UNDERCOVER
We’ve bought from 2 pharmacies – they would only sell us two bottle at a time. Then from a spaza shop we were able to buy more at a time. And then lastly, we’re buying a box from Terence’s contact.

We’ll confront the spaza shop and the box supplier.

MEDICAL EXPERT
Dr. Prikash Naidoo is a medical practitioner at ARCA Durban – he deals with codeine addiction on a daily basis. He will speak to the medical complications, long term affects and challenges with coming clean.

EXPERTS
PSSA – PHARMACEUTICAL SOCIETY OF SOUTH AFRICA – they are pushing the Codeine Care Initiative, are serious about regulating the industry and codeine distribution and will comment on the international context – they blame the SAPC

SAPC – SOUTH AFRICAN PHARMACY COUNCIL – they are the stumbling block to the codeine register implementation – they have been on it since 2010 but come up with excuse after excuse. PSSA public criticises them. (right of reply interview)

HISTORY // HIP HOP CULTURE
The mixture has been a fad in America for over 10 years, with Hip-Hop artists such as Future and Lil Wayne all rapping about it and publically consuming it – locally artists like Emtee also featured it in his music videos and has recently admitted to taking it.

Rapper Lil Wayne is also widely associated with the codeine-based drink, and in March 2013 was admitted to hospital after having a sizzurp binge which resulted in him having seizures.
There seems to be this culture behind the drink that requires one to consume it from a polystyrene cup. In addition to that, there is also the culture of having it ‘double-cupped’, meaning that you double up the polystyrene cups that you drink it from.
WHAT IS CODEINE?
Codeine (3-methylmorphine) is the most commonly consumed opiate in the world - It’s a centrally active, low-efficacy opioid or narcotic analgesic. Translation: codeine works via the central nervous system to relieve pain, but it could be addictive. And is mostly used for pain management and cough suppression.
Codeine, is a narcotic that gives you a sense of calm and wellbeing, which makes it attractive even after pain or a cough has been relieved. As your body becomes used to codeine, increased doses are taken in order to achieve this same desired effect which is where the danger of addiction to and misuse of codeine comes in.
In South Africa it is available in over-the-counter combination preparations with caffeine, paracetamol or ibuprofen or as a prescription medicine. . It can be found in a range of cough mixtures like, Benylin C, Expectalin, Goldgesic, Stilpane, Broncleer to name a few.

It’s said to be a precursor to Heroine – and has similar effects on the body according Dr. Prikash Naidoo who runs a rehab centre in Durban.

WHY WORRY?
South African National Council on Alcoholism (Sanca) director Walter Petersen said purple drank is an old drug that’s now come in a new packet.
Cough syrup is normally meant for certain ailments and it is safe to use, however, codeine is a “downer” and is high in caffeine. Codeine has abuse potential because of its opiate effect and development of tolerance in a short timeframe. Prolonged use is strongly associated with depression.
By mixing it with fizzy drinks absorption is sped up, which boosts their high. What users don’t realise is that they are damaging their liver and if this sort of drug is taken excessively it could also damage the brain.
Codeine can interact with other substances, leading to respiratory problems and other negative effects on the central nervous system. Users run the risk of going into a coma, suffering from respiratory-related illnesses, cyanosis (turning blue due to lack of oxygen), hypertension and convulsions.

Long-term or excessive use of combination products containing ibuprofen and paracetamol together with codeine can lead to problems such as gastric ulcers and inflammatory bowel conditions.

Press Release:


Codeine Cocktail Addiction
It’s easy to get, easy to hide and even easier to get hooked on. Codeine-based cough mixtures are the latest source for a high for South African youth. A simple cocktail of cough mixture – which is available over the counter for less than R50 – and a soft drink, makes a dangerous and highly addictive drug that experts describe as a precursor to polysubstance abuse. Carte Blanche investigates the cracks in the system and exposes some of the dodgy pharmaceutical suppliers putting teenagers at risk of a dangerous addiction.
Producer: Nicky Troll
Presenter: Devi Sankaree Govender
Watch the trailer


Script:


STRUCTURE

VO: Kids around the world are hooked on a codeine laced cooldrink cocktail and South Africa is not immune.

JEROME: It gives you a confident feeling, you feel strong, you feel powerful, but you’re not realizing it’s destroying you.

VO: He’s talking about Lean, Dirty Sprite, Sizzurp, Purple Drank… call it what you want, but it all comes down the same dangerous mix – it’s gripping youngsters.

LINK: The key ingredient – codeine based cough mixture - available over the counter from pharmacies. It’s easy to get. It’s easy to hide. And it’s easy to get hooked on.

VO: Popularised by international Hip Hop Culture, cough syrup has become “cool” – rappers sip from doubled-up polystyrene cups while living the so-called dream.

Psychiatrist Dr. Laurel King specialises in drug addiction, she notes the trend is picked up across a wide spectrum of youth.

DR KING: We are seeing it across all spectrums of society – in our townships, in our average middle-income groups and in our high-income population groups.

VO: It’s a concoction of cooldrink mixed with dangerously high-levels of codeine cough syrup - initially delivering a chilled euphoric state of mind.

The long-term effects of codeine abuse, are a lot more severe.

DR KING: high dosages of codeine could include things like respiratory depression, so your lungs and breathing ability decreases, it can have an effect on your neurological system in terms of impairing your psycho motive activity - you could even have cardiac arrest in lethal doses of codeine – that’s how lethal it is.

LINK: This is not an uncommon scene in Wentworth... used codeine cough mixture bottles lying everywhere. Kids are proud of their addiction - up their street cred

VO: Jerome is a grade 11 learner in Wentworth, a suburb just south of Durban.

JEROME: you want to show off to the people around you – because that’s what this drug does, if you see a youngster with a two litre, very few are drinking mineral – most of them are drinking cough mixture.

VO: He’s been using codeine syrups recreationally since the age of 15 – at one stage, taking up to 6 bottles a day, costing around R300 excluding the cooldrink.

DEVI: Where do you get the money from?
JEROME: when you on this thing, when you addicted to you’ll do anything to get it INT1 M7you steal from your house, even your closest friends.

LINK: Internationally countries from the America to Japan to Nigeria require prescriptions for medicines containing codeine, regulating the use and making it harder for addicts to abuse, but this is apparently not an option for South Africa.

VO: Dr. Johann Kruger from the Pharmaceutical Society of South Africa, believes banning over the counter sales would have a huge impact on the healthcare of average South Africans.

DR KRUGER: If we say 2% of the population is being harmed by that, 98% of the population is being advantaged by that

VO: Codeine-containing medicine effectively and legitimately treats a range of day-to-day ailments and is currently subject to regulations in South Africa.

Pharmacies are only allowed to dispense 100ml of codeine-based cough syrup. Because it is a Scheduled 2 medication – only registered and licensed individuals may dispense it and a record must be kept of the buyer’s name, address and ID number.

Interested to see how easy it is to feed this addiction – we sent in an operative to a pharmacy in Durban.

AGENT: Do you have Broncleer?
GOGGO: yes
AGENT: Can I have two?
GOGGO: yes
AGENT: How much is it mama?
GOGGO: R35 each.
AGENT: 07:08 Would I be able to get three?
GOGGO: 07:16 I dont know,because that is not allowed, but I will put in another.

VO: The agent was never asked for any details, and walked away with three bottles of codeine cough syrup – three times the legal limit. Besides breaking the law, the pharmacy is enabling addicts.

DR KING: It’s highly addictive, it’s very dangerous in over dosage, the withdrawal symptoms are very uncomfortable.

LINK: Codeine is an opiate – the most commonly used in the world – it’s in the same class of chemical as morphine and the illegal drug heroin – Just because it’s in a medicine bottle doesn’t take away the effects of dependence.

DR KING: It may be that heroine and morphine will considered the Rolls Royce of the opioid family and Codeine is maybe the Toyota Corolla, so it’s much cheaper, it’s more widely available, but it is just as lethal and as toxic in over dose as heroine and morphine.

VO: But because it’s not alcohol or hard street drugs, youngsters seem to be oblivious to the consequences.

Musician Sunny Zondi, has been clean for three months. While he was a star pupil in high school at a well known all boys school, he started experimenting then - but really got hooked after he matriculated.

SUNNY: I didn’t even know it was a drug – I didn’t even know how serious it was until I actually got kicked out home and people started making a huge thing about it – I actually didn’t know // because it’s just cough mixture.

VO: Besides the trip, it’s all about image says Sunny.

SUNNY: It became very obsessive, every time we’d get it, we’d post it on our Instagram, on our whatsapp statuses, on fb – it’s cool to actually do - that’s what you think

VO: And with the growing demand, suppliers aren’t limited to pharmacies.

SUNNY: They actually selling it in townships now, in townships as well, spaza shops – guys are getting it in bulk. If you are getting it at the pharmacy it’s like R25, if you’re gonna at the spaza or some other connection you get it for R50.

VO: We wanted to see if we could get our hands on a big order of cough syrup outside of a pharmacy, we went undercover in Chesterville, a Durban township. We met up with a supplier called Wele.

Operative: 02:32 Can I have the 'Stuff'//
Seller 02:35 How many?
Operative 02 :36 thirty-two //
Seller 03 :51 Twenty ?
Operative: 03:52 No,i want the stock-give me thirty.
Seller 03:58 I am avoiding a situation whereby people come and I don’t have.

VO: He disappeared around the front of the property and returned with a backpack full of cough mixture. They agreed on 30 bottles at a price of R1450.

Clearly this sale was not legal. The police accompanied us to Wele’s place.

DEVI: Hello?! Hello Mami!
POLICE: Open the door ma’am it’s the police!
LADY: for what?
DEVI: Looking for Wele, where’s Wele?
POLICE: Come outside ma’am - It’s the police….
DEVI: Do you know what he’s doing here? He’s selling things he’s not meant to be selling.

VO: The police searched the property occupied by Wele’s sister, but it appears the stock was moved.

LINK: There’s no sign of Wele, that is not a pharmacy, and I doubt Wele is a qualified pharmacist.

VO: But Scala Pharmacy, where we bought the three bottles of cough mixture, is definitely registered and should be operating within the law.

DEVI: You only supposed to give one, 100 ml… what you’ve been doing…
GOGGO: What’s schedule is it?
DEVI: Schedule 2.
GOGGO: I didn’t know… what we know…
DEVI: you can’t say I did know – that’s not good enough…
DEVI: // on the footage, you said I’m not supposed to sell you three – so you knew that but you still sold it. Are you with me?
GOGGO: I don’t remember, I cant remember saying that…..

VO: Strike one…Let us remind you of what happened a few weeks earlier….

AGENT: 07:08 Would I be able to get three?
GOGGO: 07:16 I dont know, because that is not allowed, but I will put in another.

DEVI: Are you a registered pharmacist assistant?
GOGGO: As in a certificate?
DEVI: Yes, as in a certificate.
GOGGO: No…..

VO: And that’s strike two…

DEVI: You’re supposed to keep a register. Where’s the register?
GOGGO: We don’t keep any…
DEVI: Why not?
GOGGO: I don’t know…

VO: With three strikes – we went looking for her manager in the office.

UPSOUND DEVI: Come, come…..

VO: Suddenly there were multiple versions and blaming left, right and centre.

UPSOUND….talking over each other

DEVI: Are you listening to yourselves all of you?
GOGGO: Yes, I’m listening to myself.
DEVI: Do you understand that this feeds a codeine addiction? SCALA CONFRONT2 M3
DEVI: Is she allowed to dispense this?
DEVENDRI: No, she’s not….
DEVI: Did she dispense this? Yes!
DEVENDRI: NODS
DEVI: Did she dispense one? NO! Did she dispense three? Yes!
DEVENDRI: NODS
DEVI: Is she breaking the law? Yes!
DEVENDRI: NODS
DEVI: Are you breaking the law? Yes!
DEVENDRI: NODS
DEVI: Right or wrong? Correct me?
DEVENDRI: agrees….

VO: The South African Pharmacy Council regulates pharmacists and pharmacy premises - Amos Masango is the Registrar & CEO.

DEVI: I feel like I was doing your job in Durban
MASANGO: No, we have inspectors
DEVI: I’m not sure what your inspectors are doing
MASANGO: When they go there we have questionnaires for inspections
DEVI: The only way to catch people is to see what they do – not to get them to fill questionnaires… nobody is going to admit to selling two or three bottles – they don’t even keep the schedule 2 register as it is.
MASANGO: That is what the law actually says…
DEVI: But a law is only as good as it’s enforcement.. you’re not enforcing anything..
MASANGO: We do.
DEVI: you’re not enforcing this.

VO: The Codeine Care Initiative was set to provide better control mechanisms by linking pharmacies and patients through a national database.

DEVI: what happened to it?
DR KRUGER: the problem – voluntary program – pharmacist voluntarily enrol, uptake very slow.
DEVI: What about doing the right thing?
DR KRUGER: They say they all have a schedule 2 register which is the minimum standard but that does not work… we have seen that.

VO: But without enforced regulations, addicts will continue to exploit the cracks in the system to get their fix. Dr. King believes the bigger issue is what happens when addiction escalates.

DR KING: they develop tolerance, and then they need more or a higher dose of the same drug to get the same effect, and they start looking for the next best fix, or the next best high and that’s where the poly substance abuse enters the fray

VO: A trend already rife in Jerome’s circles – kids have started to add Anti-depressants to the mix.

JEROME: Xanax is most popular in school and even in my school it’s like a common thing, a lot of people my age and maybe even younger take it.

DEVI: What if nothing is done to rectify this?
DR KING: There will a downward social drift, it’s a domino effect and if we don’t do anything about it now, I shudder to think what the next generation will be like.

Carte Blanche HD nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 20 November 2018 Press Release: Codeine Cocktail Addiction It’s easy to get, easy to hide and even easier to get hooked on. Codeine-based cough mixtures are the latest source for a high for South African youth. A simple cocktail of cough mixture – which is available over the counter for less than R50 – and a soft drink, makes a dangerous and highly addictive drug that experts describe as a precursor to polysubstance abuse. Carte Blanche investigates the cracks in the system and exposes some of the dodgy pharmaceutical suppliers putting teenagers at risk of a dangerous addiction. Producer: Nicky Troll Presenter: Devi Sankaree Govender Watch the trailer Script: STRUCTURE VO: Kids around the world are hooked on a codeine laced cooldrink cocktail and South Africa is not immune. JEROME: It gives you a confident feeling, you feel strong, you feel powerful, but you’re not realizing it’s destroying you. VO: He’s talking about Lean, Dirty Sprite, Sizzurp, Purple Drank… call it what you want, but it all comes down the same dangerous mix – it’s gripping youngsters. LINK: The key ingredient – codeine based cough mixture - available over the counter from pharmacies. It’s easy to get. It’s easy to hide. And it’s easy to get hooked on. VO: Popularised by international Hip Hop Culture, cough syrup has become “cool” – rappers sip from doubled-up polystyrene cups while living the so-called dream. Psychiatrist Dr. Laurel King specialises in drug addiction, she notes the trend is picked up across a wide spectrum of youth. DR KING: We are seeing it across all spectrums of society – in our townships, in our average middle-income groups and in our high-income population groups. VO: It’s a concoction of cooldrink mixed with dangerously high-levels of codeine cough syrup - initially delivering a chilled euphoric state of mind. The long-term effects of codeine abuse, are a lot more severe. DR KING: high dosages of codeine could include things like respiratory depression, so your lungs and breathing ability decreases, it can have an effect on your neurological system in terms of impairing your psycho motive activity - you could even have cardiac arrest in lethal doses of codeine – that’s how lethal it is. LINK: This is not an uncommon scene in Wentworth... used codeine cough mixture bottles lying everywhere. Kids are proud of their addiction - up their street cred VO: Jerome is a grade 11 learner in Wentworth, a suburb just south of Durban. JEROME: you want to show off to the people around you – because that’s what this drug does, if you see a youngster with a two litre, very few are drinking mineral – most of them are drinking cough mixture. VO: He’s been using codeine syrups recreationally since the age of 15 – at one stage, taking up to 6 bottles a day, costing around R300 excluding the cooldrink. DEVI: Where do you get the money from? JEROME: when you on this thing, when you addicted to you’ll do anything to get it INT1 M7you steal from your house, even your closest friends. LINK: Internationally countries from the America to Japan to Nigeria require prescriptions for medicines containing codeine, regulating the use and making it harder for addicts to abuse, but this is apparently not an option for South Africa. VO: Dr. Johann Kruger from the Pharmaceutical Society of South Africa, believes banning over the counter sales would have a huge impact on the healthcare of average South Africans. DR KRUGER: If we say 2% of the population is being harmed by that, 98% of the population is being advantaged by that VO: Codeine-containing medicine effectively and legitimately treats a range of day-to-day ailments and is currently subject to regulations in South Africa. Pharmacies are only allowed to dispense 100ml of codeine-based cough syrup. Because it is a Scheduled 2 medication – only registered and licensed individuals may dispense it and a record must be kept of the buyer’s name, address and ID number. Interested to see how easy it is to feed this addiction – we sent in an operative to a pharmacy in Durban. AGENT: Do you have Broncleer? GOGGO: yes AGENT: Can I have two? GOGGO: yes AGENT: How much is it mama? GOGGO: R35 each. AGENT: 07:08 Would I be able to get three? GOGGO: 07:16 I dont know,because that is not allowed, but I will put in another. VO: The agent was never asked for any details, and walked away with three bottles of codeine cough syrup – three times the legal limit. Besides breaking the law, the pharmacy is enabling addicts. DR KING: It’s highly addictive, it’s very dangerous in over dosage, the withdrawal symptoms are very uncomfortable. LINK: Codeine is an opiate – the most commonly used in the world – it’s in the same class of chemical as morphine and the illegal drug heroin – Just because it’s in a medicine bottle doesn’t take away the effects of dependence. DR KING: It may be that heroine and morphine will considered the Rolls Royce of the opioid family and Codeine is maybe the Toyota Corolla, so it’s much cheaper, it’s more widely available, but it is just as lethal and as toxic in over dose as heroine and morphine. VO: But because it’s not alcohol or hard street drugs, youngsters seem to be oblivious to the consequences. Musician Sunny Zondi, has been clean for three months. While he was a star pupil in high school at a well known all boys school, he started experimenting then - but really got hooked after he matriculated. SUNNY: I didn’t even know it was a drug – I didn’t even know how serious it was until I actually got kicked out home and people started making a huge thing about it – I actually didn’t know // because it’s just cough mixture. VO: Besides the trip, it’s all about image says Sunny. SUNNY: It became very obsessive, every time we’d get it, we’d post it on our Instagram, on our whatsapp statuses, on fb – it’s cool to actually do - that’s what you think VO: And with the growing demand, suppliers aren’t limited to pharmacies. SUNNY: They actually selling it in townships now, in townships as well, spaza shops – guys are getting it in bulk. If you are getting it at the pharmacy it’s like R25, if you’re gonna at the spaza or some other connection you get it for R50. VO: We wanted to see if we could get our hands on a big order of cough syrup outside of a pharmacy, we went undercover in Chesterville, a Durban township. We met up with a supplier called Wele. Operative: 02:32 Can I have the 'Stuff'// Seller 02:35 How many? Operative 02 :36 thirty-two // Seller 03 :51 Twenty ? Operative: 03:52 No,i want the stock-give me thirty. Seller 03:58 I am avoiding a situation whereby people come and I don’t have. VO: He disappeared around the front of the property and returned with a backpack full of cough mixture. They agreed on 30 bottles at a price of R1450. Clearly this sale was not legal. The police accompanied us to Wele’s place. DEVI: Hello?! Hello Mami! POLICE: Open the door ma’am it’s the police! LADY: for what? DEVI: Looking for Wele, where’s Wele? POLICE: Come outside ma’am - It’s the police…. DEVI: Do you know what he’s doing here? He’s selling things he’s not meant to be selling. VO: The police searched the property occupied by Wele’s sister, but it appears the stock was moved. LINK: There’s no sign of Wele, that is not a pharmacy, and I doubt Wele is a qualified pharmacist. VO: But Scala Pharmacy, where we bought the three bottles of cough mixture, is definitely registered and should be operating within the law. DEVI: You only supposed to give one, 100 ml… what you’ve been doing… GOGGO: What’s schedule is it? DEVI: Schedule 2. GOGGO: I didn’t know… what we know… DEVI: you can’t say I did know – that’s not good enough… DEVI: // on the footage, you said I’m not supposed to sell you three – so you knew that but you still sold it. Are you with me? GOGGO: I don’t remember, I cant remember saying that….. VO: Strike one…Let us remind you of what happened a few weeks earlier…. AGENT: 07:08 Would I be able to get three? GOGGO: 07:16 I dont know, because that is not allowed, but I will put in another. DEVI: Are you a registered pharmacist assistant? GOGGO: As in a certificate? DEVI: Yes, as in a certificate. GOGGO: No….. VO: And that’s strike two… DEVI: You’re supposed to keep a register. Where’s the register? GOGGO: We don’t keep any… DEVI: Why not? GOGGO: I don’t know… VO: With three strikes – we went looking for her manager in the office. UPSOUND DEVI: Come, come….. VO: Suddenly there were multiple versions and blaming left, right and centre. UPSOUND….talking over each other DEVI: Are you listening to yourselves all of you? GOGGO: Yes, I’m listening to myself. DEVI: Do you understand that this feeds a codeine addiction? SCALA CONFRONT2 M3 DEVI: Is she allowed to dispense this? DEVENDRI: No, she’s not…. DEVI: Did she dispense this? Yes! DEVENDRI: NODS DEVI: Did she dispense one? NO! Did she dispense three? Yes! DEVENDRI: NODS DEVI: Is she breaking the law? Yes! DEVENDRI: NODS DEVI: Are you breaking the law? Yes! DEVENDRI: NODS DEVI: Right or wrong? Correct me? DEVENDRI: agrees…. VO: The South African Pharmacy Council regulates pharmacists and pharmacy premises - Amos Masango is the Registrar & CEO. DEVI: I feel like I was doing your job in Durban MASANGO: No, we have inspectors DEVI: I’m not sure what your inspectors are doing MASANGO: When they go there we have questionnaires for inspections DEVI: The only way to catch people is to see what they do – not to get them to fill questionnaires… nobody is going to admit to selling two or three bottles – they don’t even keep the schedule 2 register as it is. MASANGO: That is what the law actually says… DEVI: But a law is only as good as it’s enforcement.. you’re not enforcing anything.. MASANGO: We do. DEVI: you’re not enforcing this. VO: The Codeine Care Initiative was set to provide better control mechanisms by linking pharmacies and patients through a national database. DEVI: what happened to it? DR KRUGER: the problem – voluntary program – pharmacist voluntarily enrol, uptake very slow. DEVI: What about doing the right thing? DR KRUGER: They say they all have a schedule 2 register which is the minimum standard but that does not work… we have seen that. VO: But without enforced regulations, addicts will continue to exploit the cracks in the system to get their fix. Dr. King believes the bigger issue is what happens when addiction escalates. DR KING: they develop tolerance, and then they need more or a higher dose of the same drug to get the same effect, and they start looking for the next best fix, or the next best high and that’s where the poly substance abuse enters the fray VO: A trend already rife in Jerome’s circles – kids have started to add Anti-depressants to the mix. JEROME: Xanax is most popular in school and even in my school it’s like a common thing, a lot of people my age and maybe even younger take it. DEVI: What if nothing is done to rectify this? DR KING: There will a downward social drift, it’s a domino effect and if we don’t do anything about it now, I shudder to think what the next generation will be like.
